content.title: About
content.content: Chicken, fried in a coating, consists of pieces of chicken meat covered with breadcrumbs or batter and deep‑fried until golden and crisp. Both the skin and the coating are edible, providing a crunchy texture and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fried chicken is one of the most popular dishes worldwide and has countless regional variations.
Coatings can include spices, herbs, cheese, nuts or panko, allowing endless flavor combinations.
Chicken meat is high in protein, while the crispy crust adds a pleasant textural contrast.
Traditionally served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, or spicy chili.
In some cuisines the chicken is fried in oil infused with aromatics like rosemary or thyme.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fried chicken supplies niacin (B3), vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein and moderate fat content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Regular consumption combined with exercise can help maintain and build lean muscle.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories; people watching their weight should control portion size.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Reusing oil can create trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may have an allergic reaction to chicken proteins.

items.title: Foodborne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried chicken can be enjoyed on its own, added to salads, sandwiches, wraps, or served with sides such as mashed potatoes, rice, or vegetables. Cut into bite‑size pieces for children.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fried chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before eating.
